sentences: When Prince Anpyeong, third son of King Sejong, described a paradise he had seen in a dream, court painter An Gyeon turned it into this scroll in three days.

Most East Asian handscrolls read right to left, but this one starts with the ordinary world at the left, climbs through jagged rocky mountains, and arrives at a valley of blossoming peach trees on the right.
Several viewpoints are stitched seamlessly together, so viewing it feels like walking through a dream.
Attached after the painting are the prince's own text and poems by some twenty of the finest scholars of the day, making it a time capsule of early Joseon culture at its height.
It is now in Japan and has been shown in Korea only on rare occasions.
